title: Profiling individual through inferred health conditions
description: The app analyzes user data to infer eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, creating profiles that link data to specific individuals through pattern analysis.
assumptions: The app has access to sufficient historical health data to perform meaningful inference

title: Quasi-identifier combination through health indicators
description: Health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) combined with other user attributes could serve as quasi-identifiers that link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Health indicators are combined with other user data that could be used for re-identification

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to user
description: The dashboard displays revealing health attributes (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) that directly identify the user's health status and condition.
assumptions: Health condition indicators are considered revealing personal attributes

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The app processes identified health data to generate and display condition indicators to the user.
assumptions: The system processes data that is linked to specific identified users

title: Sensitive health data type disclosure
description: The app displays highly sensitive health data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) which may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic app functionality.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: The app performs analysis and enrichment of health data to create risk signals, which may exceed what is functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The inference/analysis of health conditions may not be strictly necessary for the app's stated purpose

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being analyzed, what inferences are being made, or how risk signals are generated.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of data analysis performed on their health information

title: Lack of user control over health data processing preferences
description: Users may lack control over preferences regarding how their health data is processed, analyzed, and what risk indicators are displayed.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular consent or preference controls for health data processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health data to generate risk signals may process more personal data than actually needed for the app's functional goals.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only data strictly necessary for the purpose

title: Automated decision making on sensitive personal data
description: The app uses automated analysis to infer health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk), which may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: Health risk inference qualifies as automated decision-making on sensitive data under GDPR
uncertainty_note: Assumes the inference algorithms qualify as automated decision-making under applicable regulations
